action: Students and parents: do not pay anyone offering VCE exam papers; the VCAA says the claims are false. Rely on official VCAA channels for exam information.
exec: A confirmed website defacement during exam season; the more serious exam-theft claim is unverified and denied by the authority.
impact: The authority's corporate website was offline while it investigated.
plain: A hacker vandalised the website of Victoria's school exam authority and claimed to be selling exam papers. The authority says the exam claims are false.
summary: The VCAA's website was taken down on November 12, during Victoria's exam period, after a hacker calling themselves DaggerElite replaced its front page with a message claiming exam papers were stolen through external printers and sold to students. The VCAA confirms the defacement but says there is no evidence exams or sensitive data were accessed and calls the claims fabricated. Exams continue as normal.
title: Hacker defaces Victorian exam authority's website and claims to have sold exam papers

validation.note: One outlet quoting the VCAA chief executive; the exam-theft claim is unconfirmed.
